source_text: Tales etiamsi occisi in confessione nominis fuerint, macula ista nec sanguine abluitur: inexpiabilis et gravis culpa discordiae nec passione purgatur. Esse martyr non potest qui in Ecclesia non est: ad regnum pervenire non poterit qui eam quae regnatura est derelinquit. Pacem nobis Christus dedit, concordes atque unanimes esse praecepit, dilectionis et charitatis foedera incorrupta atque inviolata servari mandavit. Exhibere se non potest martyrem qui fraternam non tenuit charitatem. Docet hoc et contestatur Paulus apostolus dicens: Et si habuero fidem ita ut montes transferam, charitatem autem non habeam, nihil sum. Et si in cibos pauperum distribuero omnia mea, et si tradidero corpus meum ut ardeam, charitatem autem non habeam, nihil proficio. Charitas magnanima est, charitas benigna est, charitas non aemulatur, non agit perperam, non inflatur, non irritatur, non cogitat malum, omnia diligit, omnia credit, omnia sperat, omnia sustinet. Charitas numquam excidit. Numquam, inquit, excidit charitas. Haec enim semper in regno erit, haec in aeternum fraternitatis sibi cohaerentis unitate durabit. Ad regnum coelorum non potest pervenire discordia; ad praemia Christi, qui dixit, Hoc est mandatum meum, ut diligatis invicem, quemadmodum dilexi vos, pertinere non poterit qui dilectionem Christi perfida dissensione violavit. Qui charitatem non habet, Deum non habet. Joannis beati apostoli vox est: Deus, inquit, dilectio est; et qui manet in dilectione, in Deo manet, et Deus in illo manet. Cum Deo manere non possunt qui esse in Ecclesia Dei unanimes noluerunt. Ardeant licet flammis et ignibus traditi vel objecti bestiis animas suas ponant, non erit illa fidei corona, sed poena perfidiae; nec religiosae virtutis exitus gloriosus, sed desperationis interitus. Occidi talis potest, coronari non potest. Sic se christianum esse profitetur quomodo et Christum diabolus saepe mentitur, ipso Domino praemonente et dicente: Multi venient in nomine meo dicentes: Ego sum Christus, et multos fallent. Sicut ille Christus non est, quamvis fallat in nomine, ita nec christianus videri potest qui non permanet in Evangelii ejus et fidei veritate.
pass_a_gloss: Even if such people are killed in the confession of the name, this stain is not washed away by blood: the inexpiable and grave fault of discord is not purified by passion. One who is not in the Church cannot be a martyr: one who abandons the Church, which will reign, cannot arrive at the kingdom. Christ gave us peace, commanded us to be in harmony and of one mind, and ordered that the pact of love and charity be kept incorrupt and inviolate. One who did not maintain fraternal charity cannot exhibit himself as a martyr. The apostle Paul teaches and testifies to this, saying: And if I have faith so that I can move mountains, but I do not have charity, I am nothing. And if I distribute all my goods to the poor, and if I hand over my body to be burned, but I do not have charity, I gain nothing. Charity is magnanimous, charity is kind, charity does not envy, does not act wrongly, is not inflated, is not irritated, does not think evil, loves all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Charity never fails. Never, he says, does charity fail. For this will always be in the kingdom, this will endure in the eternal unity of fraternal concord. Discord cannot arrive at the kingdom of heaven; one who violates Christ's love with perfidious dissension cannot belong to Christ's rewards, who said: This is my commandment, that you love one another, just as I loved you. One who does not have charity does not have God. The voice of the blessed apostle John is: God, he says, is love; and one who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him. Those who did not want to be in harmony in the Church of God cannot remain with God. Even if they are handed over to flames and fires, or if they lay down their lives, having been thrown to the beasts, it will not be the crown of faith, but the punishment of perfidy; nor the glorious outcome of religious virtue, but the destruction of desperation. Such a person can be killed, but cannot be crowned. Thus one who claims to be a Christian, just as the devil often lies, saying that he is Christ, with the Lord himself warning and saying: Many will come in my name, saying: I am Christ, and they will deceive many. Just as he is not Christ, although he deceives in the name, so also one who does not remain in the truth of his Gospel and faith cannot be seen as a Christian.
pass_b_english: Even if such people are killed confessing the name, that stain is not washed away by blood; the inexpiable and grave fault of discord is not purified by suffering. (1 Cor 13:2–3) No one who is not in the Church can be a martyr, and no one who abandons the Church, which is destined to reign, can arrive at the kingdom. Christ gave us peace, commanded us to be harmonious and of one mind, and ordered that the covenant of love and charity be kept incorrupt and inviolate. Anyone who did not hold fast to brotherly charity cannot present himself as a martyr. The apostle Paul teaches and testifies to this when he says: if I have faith so as to move mountains but do not have charity, I am nothing; and if I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I hand over my body to be burned, but do not have charity, I gain nothing. (1 Cor 13:2–3) Charity is magnanimous, charity is kind; charity does not envy, does not act shamefully, is not puffed up, is not provoked, does not count up wrongs; it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Charity never fails. Never, he says, does charity fail. For it will always remain in the kingdom; it will endure forever in the unbroken unity of brotherly concord. (1 Cor 13:4–8) Discord cannot enter the kingdom of heaven; the one who violates Christ's love with perfidious division cannot share in the rewards of Christ, who said, "This is my commandment, that you love one another, just as I have loved you." (John 13:34) Whoever lacks charity lacks God. The voice of the blessed apostle John declares: "God is love, and whoever remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him." (1 John 4:16) Those who refused to live in harmony in the Church of God cannot remain with God. Even if they are delivered to flames and fire, or thrown to the beasts and lay down their lives, the result will not be the crown of faith but the punishment of faithlessness; not the glorious outcome of religious virtue but the destruction of despair. Such a person can be killed, but cannot be crowned. Thus someone professes to be a Christian just as the devil often lies, claiming to be Christ himself, despite the Lord's own warning: "Many will come in my name, saying, 'I am the Christ,' and they will deceive many." (Matt 24:5) Just as that one is not the Christ though he deceives in the name, so also the one who does not remain in the truth of his Gospel and faith cannot be recognized as a Christian.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering with appropriate scripture citations (1 Cor 13:2–3, John 13:34, 1 John 4:16, Matt 24:5) that match the quoted/alluded content. All clauses, including the complex conditional structures regarding martyrdom and the devil's deception, are preserved.
